title: How Money Became God: Online Author Talk with Paul Vigna
description: 12:00 PM – 1:00 PM · Join us for an eye-opening conversation with veteran journalist Paul Vigna as we examine his provocative book, The Almightier: How Money Became God, Greed Became Virtue, and Debt Became Sin , in which he explores the question: how did money go from a tool of commerce into the dominant faith of modern society? In The Almightier , Vigna takes readers on a sweeping historical journey from Renaissance Florence to today's global financial markets, revealing how wealth accumulation evolved from a moral failing into an unspoken civic virtue. He uncovers the forgotten history of money, tracing the uneasy and often accidental alliance between wealth and religion as it developed from ancient city-states to today's secular world, where religious devotion has receded and greed has stepped in to fill the void. …

title: Lite Lunch-Exit Party
description: 12:00 PM – 1:00 PM · NEW YORK TIMES BESTSELLER • The award-winning, bestselling author of Station Eleven and Sea of Tranquility returns with a breathtaking novel of doubles, shadow worlds, and fractured timelines as a man disappears from a glittering Los Angeles party, and a woman—a gunrunner, an art collector, an operative of the State—searches for answers. "The only world-builder more efficient than Mandel may be God. . . . Exit Party is the kind of novel you'll be desperate to talk about." —Ron Charles Los Angeles, 2031: The first spring after the collapse of the United States, peacekeeping troops withdraw from the city, the Jacaranda trees blossom, and the curfew is finally lifted. Ari Waker and her roommate pass the gauntlet of bomb-sniffing dogs, the shanty towns, and the Red Cross tents as they walk across Silverlake to a party. …

title: Radio Biblioteca
description: A bilingual library program broadcast from KOTO Radio Station, Radio Biblioteca shares local news and community events in both Spanish and English. The program is presented by Wilkinson Public Library in partnership with KOTO 91.7 FM.

title: Mahjongg for Independent Players
description: 1:00 PM – 3:00 PM · Looking to enjoy an afternoon of friendly games of mah-jongg for independent players? Join us at the Library every Wednesday from 1-3pm. Bring your 2026 card if you have one, although we have plenty of loaners if you don't! We'll have tables, cloths, chairs, and sets.   NOTE: This is not a mah-jongg lesson. A general knowledge of the game is necessary to join. Please register in advance if you'd like to join so we can make sure we have enough tables set up for everyone!

title: Movie and A Snack Club
description: A free library program held in the Program Room at Wilkinson Public Library, where participants gather to watch a movie and enjoy a snack. The event runs from 3:30 to 5:30 PM.

title: Teen Reimagine Our Community
description: A teen program at Wilkinson Public Library's Teen Area centered on a conversation series called "Reimagining Our Community," where participants explore fictional scenarios designed to spark discussion around challenging topics in a supportive environment. The series aims to foster growth, healing, and community connection among Telluride's teen population.

title: Sewing 101 with Melissa
description: 5:00 PM – 7:00 PM · Don't throw away your old clothes just because they have a tiny (or even a large) hole in them! Learn the basics of sewing and mending your clothing with our very own talented seamstress, Melissa Sumpter! Bring your own garment, we'll provide the sewing materials.

title: Dudes Who Read Book Club: All Quiet on the Western Front
description: 5:30 PM – 6:30 PM · Join us for Dudes Who Read , led by our very own library bookworms, Dennis and Oliver. This month, the dudes will be discussing All Quiet on the Western Front in honor of Veteran's Day. This month's meeting will be at The Patio (138 E Colorado Ave). Light snacks will be provided. Seats are limited, so make sure to sign up to secure your spot. I am young, I am twenty years old; yet I know nothing of life but despair, death, fear, and fatuous superficiality cast over an abyss of sorrow. . . . This is the testament of Paul Bäumer, who enlists with his classmates in the German army during World War I. They become soldiers with youthful enthusiasm. But the world of duty, culture, and progress they had been taught breaks in pieces under the first bombardment in the trenches. …
